They form when water and air pile loose sand against a barrier, such as foothills or tall mountains. Dunes grow, shrink, change shape, and move positions as water and air move around them. Some of the national parks contain large expanses of dunes, including vast tracts of white sand dunes and the tallest dunes in North America. Energy Reliability Strengthen Grid Reliability and Security Fortifying America’s electric grid is critical to the reliable and secure delivery of electricity . Under President Trump’s Executive Order, “Declaring a National Energy Emergency,” the Department will identify and exercise all lawful authorities to strengthen the nation’s grid, including the backbone of the grid, our transmission system. This is an imperative as we consider current and anticipated load growth on our nation’s electric utilities. Moreover, after two decades of very slow demand growth, electricity demand is forecast to soar in the coming years . The Department will bring a renewed focus to growing baseload and dispatchable generation to reliably meet growing demand. Skip to global NPS navigation Skip to the main content Skip to the footer section National Park Service Search Search This Site All NPS Exiting nps.gov Cancel Contact Us The Legacy of Slavery As the United States expanded from 13 colonies, the debates over chattel slavery grew—some states came to abolish it, while others refused to untangle their political, economic, and social life from the institution. With the outbreak of the Civil War in 1861, enslaved African Americans saw the war as opportunity to emancipate themselves. When President Lincoln authorized the Emancipation Proclamation, formerly enslaved African American men joined the Union army to fight for the full emancipation of their race. The conclusion of the war in Union victory and the ratification of the 13th, 14th, and 15th Amendments to the US Constitution brought African Americans closer than they ever had been to full citizenship. Nevertheless, the struggle for equality continued. Through our historical resources, the National Park Service tells these stories of African-American perseverance in the face of great adversity. The initiatives and actions below reflect FDA's commitment to engaging with manufacturers earlier, modernizing oversight tools, streamlining regulatory processes, and helping incentivize domestic investment — all while upholding FDA's rigorous standards. PreCheck Pilot Program FDA's voluntary PreCheck Pilot Program is designed to strengthen the domestic pharmaceutical supply chain by helping companies building new drug manufacturing facilities in the United States engage with the FDA earlier in the development process. The program has two phases: an early Facility Readiness Phase, where manufacturers receive technical and regulatory feedback before operations begin, and an Application Submission Phase, which includes enhanced FDA engagement to resolve manufacturing questions and expedite review of facility information and inspections. By identifying potential issues earlier, the program aims to reduce delays, improve regulatory predictability, and accelerate the availability of U.S.-manufactured medicines. Tudriqev is indicated in combination with nivolumab for the treatment of adult patients with unresectable advanced cutaneous melanoma who experienced disease progression with a programmed death receptor-1 (PD-1)-blocking antibody-based regimen. The approval is supported by data from a clinical trial showing that one in four patients responded to treatment, with responses lasting a median of nearly 14 months, offering clinicians a meaningful new tool for a patient population. In reaching this decision, the FDA also considered input from clinical experts and patient advocates who emphasized the urgent need for effective options in this refractory population. “For patients with advanced melanoma that has stopped responding to PD-1 blocking therapy, the prognosis is often devastating, and options have been far too limited. HNSCC is an aggressive, life-threatening disease for which there is a high unmet need for effective therapies. Rybrevant Faspro is not indicated as a treatment for patients with oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma that is associated with human papillomavirus (HPV). Approval was based on trial results showing that more than double the percentage of patients responded to the drug compared to currently approved therapies. pages.text: FDA PreCheck Pilot Program | FDA Skip to main content Skip to FDA Search Skip to in this section menu Skip to footer links Home For Industry FDA PreCheck Pilot Program For Industry In this section Program Overview FDA PreCheck Program represents a strategic initiative to strengthen America's pharmaceutical supply chain by reducing regulatory barriers for domestic manufacturing facilities. Currently, more than half of pharmaceuticals distributed in the U.S. are manufactured overseas, with only 11% of Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient (API) manufacturers being U.S.-based, creating significant national security vulnerabilities. In response to Executive Order 14293, "Regulatory Relief to Promote Domestic Production of Critical Medicines," FDA hopes to facilitate the development of new U.S. drug manufacturing facilities by streamlining the review and inspection process for new construction manufacturing facilities that will supply finished dosage form (FDF) or API. Phase I of the FDA PreCheck Pilot Program will select participants who are developing new pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities based on alignment to program priorities and will begin conducting FDA PreCheck activities in 2026. Companies selected for the program will benefit from FDA communication and feedback throughout the facility development process. The FDA PreCheck Pilot Program reflects FDA’s commitment to create more efficient regulatory review processes and ensure access to life-saving medicines for American patients. pages.description: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today issued final guidance for manufacturers of cellular and gene therapy (CGT) products to implement a comprehensive, science- and risk-based plan for making sure their products meet potency standards.
pages.text: FDA Provides Clarity to Support Cell and Gene Therapy Development and Quality | FDA Skip to main content Skip to FDA Search Skip to in this section menu Skip to footer links Home News & Events FDA Newsroom Press Announcements FDA Provides Clarity to Support Cell and Gene Therapy Development and Quality Press Announcements In this section More Press Announcements For Immediate Release: November 02, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today issued final guidance for manufacturers of cellular and gene therapy (CGT) products to implement a comprehensive, science- and risk-based plan for making sure their products meet potency standards. The guidance provides FDA’s recommendations for a Potency Assurance Strategy, which guides manufacturers to test and verify — before a product reaches a patient — that every batch meets a defined standard of potency to do what the product is supposed to do therapeutically. The Potency Assurance for Cellular and Gene Therapy Products final guidance replaces FDA's 2011 potency testing guidance for CGT products and applies to treatments for serious and often life-threatening conditions. By law, manufacturers are expected to verify that their products work as intended, from the time of approval through post-approval monitoring. This final guidance provides FDA’s current thinking and recommendations on how manufacturers can meet that requirement. While they may be overlooked in the shadow of spectacular mountains, they perform important ecosystem functions, providing homes for many plants and animals. These lands, which have more mild climates than the nearby peaks, protect wildlife and make a hospitable place for us to visit.
